A.explanation: Too small by a factor of 1000, from treating $150 \, \mu\text{s}$ as $150 \, \text{ms}$ or misreading $\mu\text{s}$ as $\text{ms}$.

B.explanation: Too small by a factor of 100, from an error converting cm to mm or $\mu\text{s}$ to s when finding $T$ and $f = 1/T$.

D.explanation: Too large by a factor of 10, from using about $0.3 \, \text{cm}$ instead of $3 \, \text{cm}$ for one period on the CRO screen.

hints: Look along the horizontal time axis and count how many 1 cm squares make one complete sine-wave cycle from the trace.
Remember the time-base $5 \, \mu\text{s mm}^{-1}$ means each 1 mm of horizontal length equals $5 \, \mu\text{s}$, so convert the cycle length from cm to mm first.
After you get the period $T$ in seconds, use $f = 1/T$ and check the power of 10 carefully to decide between Hz and kHz.
walkthrough: Measure one full wavelength on the screen. The repeating pattern occupies 3 horizontal squares, and each square is $1 \, \text{cm}$, so length for one period is $3.0 \, \text{cm} = 30 \, \text{mm}$.
Use the time-base to convert horizontal distance to time. $T = \text{length} \times \text{time-base} = 30 \, \text{mm} \times 5 \, \mu\text{s mm}^{-1} = 150 \, \mu\text{s}$.
